project.name: Holiday Planner
project.description: A family holiday planner: trips, day-by-day activities, budget and fair splits, packing, bookings and safe sharing, served locally by Python's standard library.

environments.title: One day's schedule and a requested slot

nodes.title: Keep every trip in one workspace

data.description: A family creates trips and finds them again in one place.
data.success_measure: A created trip is listed and opens with everything entered.

data.description: A trip's dates never contradict themselves or exceed the agreed length.
data.success_measure: No stored trip ends before it starts or lasts more than 60 days.

data.description: Each trip lists its travelers and who organizes.
data.success_measure: Every traveler appears once per trip with a role.

nodes.title: See the trip day by day

data.description: The trip is laid out as one page per calendar day.
data.success_measure: Days always match the trip's dates without losing planned activities.

data.description: Travelers place activities at a time on a day.
data.success_measure: Activities appear on their day in time order.

data.description: Two activities of the same day never overlap.
data.success_measure: No stored day holds overlapping activities, even under concurrent requests.

data.description: Expenses add up to a visible total, in whole cents.
data.success_measure: The total equals the sum of recorded expenses.

data.description: A trip over its budget is flagged as soon as it happens.
data.success_measure: Every over-budget trip shows the flag; no other trip does.

data.description: Shared expenses are split fairly and balances settle to zero.
data.success_measure: Shares always add up to the expense, to the cent.

data.description: Shared and personal packing lists everyone can check.
data.success_measure: Checked items show as packed for every traveler.

data.description: Plain-text notes per day, safe to display.
data.success_measure: Notes display exactly as typed and never run as code.

nodes.title: Find the places of the trip

data.description: Saved places with coordinates and a map link.
data.success_measure: Every saved place opens on a map at its coordinates.

data.description: Flights, stays and tickets attached to the trip, codes protected.
data.success_measure: Bookings fit the trip's dates and codes are never fully shown.

data.description: A trip moves through draft, planned, booked, completed or cancelled.
data.success_measure: Only declared status changes ever happen.

data.description: A read-only link shows the itinerary to family and friends.
data.success_measure: A link reveals nothing beyond the itinerary and stops working once revoked.

nodes.title: Take the plan into a calendar

data.description: The itinerary exports to any calendar application.
data.success_measure: The exported file imports with one event per activity.

data.description: Search across trips, activities, places and notes.
data.success_measure: A search returns every item containing the text.

nodes.title: See a day at a glance

data.description: A clear time grid for each day, usable by everyone.
data.success_measure: The day view matches the stored activities and passes the accessibility review.

data.description: Backups export and import every trip safely.
data.success_measure: A backup imports back to identical trips; a bad file changes nothing.

data.description: Health, configuration and logs an operator can trust.
data.success_measure: The health check reports storage, and logs hold no personal data.

data.trigger: a traveler creates a trip with a name, a destination and dates
data.subject: planner
data.response: store the trip and return its identifier, newest trips listed first

data.trigger: a trip name is empty or longer than 80 characters
data.subject: planner
data.response: refuse the trip with the field name and a reason code

data.trigger: a trip would end before it starts or last more than 60 days
data.subject: planner
data.response: refuse the dates without changing the trip

data.trigger: an organizer adds a traveler to a trip
data.subject: planner
data.response: store the traveler with the role organizer or companion

data.trigger: a traveler's name already exists in the trip
data.subject: planner
data.response: refuse the duplicate and keep the existing traveler

data.trigger: a trip's dates are set or changed
data.subject: planner
data.response: list one day per calendar date from start to end, keeping existing day content

data.trigger: shortening the dates would remove a day that holds activities
data.subject: planner
data.response: refuse the change and name the affected days

data.trigger: a traveler adds an activity with a title, a day, a start minute and a duration
data.subject: planner
data.response: place it on that day, ordered by start minute

data.trigger: an activity's start minute is outside 0-1439, its duration is not positive or it ends after midnight
data.subject: planner
data.response: refuse the activity with the field and a reason code

data.trigger: a new or moved activity would overlap another activity of the same day
data.subject: planner
data.response: refuse it without changing the day

data.trigger: a traveler records an expense with an amount, a payer and a category
data.subject: planner
data.response: add it to the trip's total in whole cents

data.subject: planner
data.response: show the remaining budget in cents

data.trigger: an expense amount is not a positive number of cents
data.subject: planner
data.response: refuse the expense with the field amount_cents

data.trigger: the recorded expenses exceed the trip budget
data.subject: planner
data.response: flag the trip as over budget without refusing the expense

nodes.title: Split in whole cents that add up

data.trigger: an expense is split among travelers
data.subject: planner
data.response: assign each share in whole cents so the shares add up exactly to the amount, remaining cents going to the payer

data.subject: planner
data.response: compute each traveler's balance as paid minus owed, in cents

data.trigger: an expense is split among no traveler or among someone who is not on the trip
data.subject: planner
data.response: refuse the split and keep the expense unsplit

data.trigger: a traveler adds a packing item
data.subject: planner
data.response: list the item unchecked, shared or personal as chosen

data.trigger: a traveler checks a packing item
data.subject: planner
data.response: mark it packed for everyone who sees that list

data.subject: planner
data.response: render day notes as plain text, never as HTML

data.trigger: a traveler saves a place with a name and coordinates
data.subject: planner
data.response: store latitude and longitude as integer microdegrees and offer a map link

data.trigger: a latitude is outside -90..90 degrees or a longitude outside -180..180 degrees
data.subject: planner
data.response: refuse the place with the field and a reason code

data.trigger: a traveler records a booking with a kind, dates and a confirmation code
data.subject: planner
data.response: attach it to the trip

data.subject: planner
data.response: show a confirmation code masked except its last four characters

data.trigger: a booking's dates fall outside the trip
data.subject: planner
data.response: refuse the booking with the field dates

data.trigger: a requested status change is not a declared transition
data.subject: planner
data.response: refuse it and keep the current status

data.trigger: an organizer creates a share link
data.subject: planner
data.response: issue a random token of at least 128 bits that opens a read-only itinerary

data.trigger: a share token is unknown or revoked
data.subject: planner
data.response: answer not found without revealing whether the trip exists

nodes.title: Keep money and codes out of shared views

data.subject: planner
data.response: leave expenses, balances and booking codes out of shared views

data.trigger: a traveler exports a trip
data.subject: planner
data.response: produce an iCalendar file with one event per activity, escaping text as RFC 5545 requires

data.trigger: a traveler searches with text
data.subject: planner
data.response: return the trips, activities, places and notes whose text contains it, ignoring case

data.trigger: a search term is shorter than 2 or longer than 100 characters
data.subject: planner
data.response: refuse it with the field q and a reason code

nodes.title: Show a day as a time grid

data.subject: planner
data.response: show each day as a time grid with activities sized by duration and coloured by category

data.subject: planner
data.response: keep every page usable with a keyboard alone and at WCAG 2.2 AA contrast

data.trigger: an organizer exports a backup
data.subject: planner
data.response: write every trip as JSON with a schema version, all or nothing

data.trigger: an imported backup has an unknown schema version or fails validation
data.subject: planner
data.response: refuse it without changing the stored trips

data.trigger: the health endpoint is called
data.subject: planner
data.response: answer 200 with the storage status and the version

nodes.title: Keep personal data out of logs

data.subject: planner
data.response: write logs without traveler names, notes, codes or amounts

data.subject: planner
data.response: read its port and data path from PORT and DATA_PATH, with safe local defaults

data.definition: A named journey with a destination, a start date and an end date, inclusive.
One calendar date of a trip, from start to end inclusive.
A titled item on one day, from a start minute for a positive duration, ending no later than midnight.
An integer from 0 (00:00) to 1440 (midnight at the end of the day), local to the destination.
An integer number of the trip currency's hundredths; one currency per trip.
A random string of at least 128 bits that opens one trip's read-only itinerary until revoked.
What a traveler paid minus what they owe, in cents; balances of a trip add up to zero.

nodes.title: No two activities of a day overlap
A requested slot fits the day
Shares add up to the expense
Back-to-back activities and a free slot

data.expected: The new activity is placed after lunch; touching ends are not overlaps.
The day is invalid: museum and lunch overlap by 20 minutes.
The request is refused and the day keeps only the museum.
The expense is kept and the trip is flagged over budget by 20000 cents.

nodes.title: A three-way split with a remainder

data.expected: The payer's share takes the remaining cent; shares add up to 1000.

nodes.title: A split that loses a cent

data.expected: Invalid: one cent is lost, so balances would not settle.

data.oracle: A created trip returns its identifier, reads back with every field, and lists before older trips.
Empty and 81-character names are refused with field name and reason required or too_long; nothing is stored.
An end before the start and a 61-day trip are refused; the stored trip is unchanged.
A trip of exactly 60 days is accepted and has 60 days.
PUT with an end before the start answers 400 with field end_date; a GET returns the old dates.
An organizer and a companion are stored with their roles; an unknown role is refused.
Adding Ana twice is refused with reason duplicate; the trip has one Ana.
A 3-day trip has 3 days; extending it to 5 keeps the content of the first 3.
Shortening a trip whose last day holds an activity is refused, naming that day; dates are unchanged.
Shortening a trip whose removed days are empty succeeds and drops exactly those days.

nodes.title: Planned days protected through the API

data.oracle: The API answers 409 with the affected days and the stored trip keeps its dates and activities.
Activities added at 14:00 then 09:00 list as 09:00, 14:00.
Start 1440, duration 0 and an end after midnight are each refused with their field; the day is unchanged.
Adding 09:30-10:30 to a day holding 09:00-10:00 raises Overlap and the day still holds one activity.
Activities 09:00-10:00 and 10:00-11:00 are both accepted: touching ends do not overlap.
Two simultaneous requests for overlapping slots, released together by a barrier, admit exactly one; the stored day passes CON-001.
Expenses of 400.00 and 300.00 against a 1000.00 budget give a total of 70000 and 30000 cents remaining.
Amounts 0 and -5 are refused with field amount_cents; the total is unchanged.
The flag is off within the budget and on, with the excess in cents, once expenses exceed it; no expense is refused.
1000 cents among the payer, Ana and Ben give 334, 333 and 333; the payer gets the remainder.
A split among nobody, or including someone not on the trip, is refused; the expense stays unsplit.
For 1000 seeded random amounts and traveler counts, shares always add up to the amount and differ by at most one cent.
After three split expenses, the balances endpoint returns paid minus owed per traveler and they add up to zero.
Splitting with a traveler not on the trip answers 400 and the expense stays unsplit.
A shared item checked by Ana shows packed for Ben; a personal item shows only on its owner's list.
A note holding <script> renders as the literal text <script>.
A note with accents and line breaks renders the same characters and line breaks.
The served day page shows the note's markup as text and holds no injected element.
Paris at 48.8566, 2.3522 is stored as 48856600 and 2352200 microdegrees with a map link to those coordinates.
Latitude 91 and longitude -181 are refused with their field.
A hotel booking inside the trip is attached and listed with its kind and dates.
A booking starting the day before the trip is refused with field dates.
Code ABC12345 displays as ****2345.
A code of four characters or fewer displays as **** only.

nodes.title: API never returns a full code

data.oracle: No API response body for a trip with bookings contains a full confirmation code.
completed -> draft and cancelled -> planned are refused; the status is unchanged.
draft -> planned -> booked -> completed succeeds step by step.
POST status draft on a completed trip answers 409 and the trip stays completed.
A token decodes to at least 16 random bytes; 1000 tokens are all distinct.

nodes.title: Revoked and unknown links look the same

data.oracle: A revoked token and a never-issued token both answer 404 with byte-identical bodies.

nodes.title: Shared views hold no money or codes

data.oracle: The shared itinerary holds activities and places, and no expense, balance or confirmation code.
An organizer shares a trip; the link shows its itinerary and offers no editing control.

nodes.title: Writes refused with a share token

data.oracle: Any write attempted with a share token is refused; the trip is unchanged.
A trip with three activities exports a VCALENDAR with three VEVENTs at floating local times.
Commas, semicolons, backslashes and line breaks in titles are escaped; long lines are folded at 75 octets.
Searching 'louvre' returns the activity, the place and the note that contain Louvre.
Terms of 1 and 101 characters are refused with field q.
The day page places a 90-minute activity at 09:00 over three half-hour rows, coloured by its category.
A reviewer completes every flow with the keyboard alone and measures contrast of 4.5:1 or more on text, with notes.
Every interactive element of the main pages is reachable by Tab and has a visible focus style.
Exporting then importing into an empty store gives byte-identical trip records.
A backup with schema version 99 is refused with reason unsupported_version.
An import whose third trip is invalid answers 400 and the store keeps exactly its previous trips.
An export interrupted after the first trip leaves no partial backup file.

nodes.title: Export and import through the API

data.oracle: GET /api/backup then POST it to a fresh store answers 200 and lists the same trips.
GET /health answers 200 with storage ok and the version.
A log record carrying a name, a note, a code and an amount is written without those values.
Method, path template, status and duration remain in the log line.

nodes.title: No personal data during a request

data.oracle: After creating a trip with a traveler and a note through the API, the captured logs contain none of their values.
PORT=9000 and DATA_PATH are read; without them the server uses 8000 and ./data/planner.sqlite3.

data.responsibility: Persists trips, days, activities, expenses and bookings in one SQLite file, each change in one transaction.
data.boundary: app/store.py: the only module that opens the database

data.responsibility: Validates trips, dates, activities, splits, places, bookings and status changes as pure functions.
Serves the JSON API, the pages and the health check; maps refusals to stable status codes.
Renders the trip, day timeline, shared view and forms, escaping every value.
Issues, checks and revokes share tokens and builds the shared view.
Builds iCalendar files, backups and search results.
Reads configuration and writes scrubbed structured logs.

data.question: How long may one trip last?
data.rationale: Day pages and calendar exports stay readable; longer journeys are split into trips.

data.question: Who receives the cents left over when an expense does not divide evenly?
data.rationale: The payer already advanced the money; the rule is simple to explain.

data.question: What may a read-only share link show?
options: itinerary, places and packing list, no money or codes
data.answer: itinerary, places and packing list, no money or codes
data.rationale: Family and friends need the plan, not who paid what or booking codes.

data.question: Which time do exported calendar events use?
options: floating local time at the destination
data.answer: floating local time at the destination
data.rationale: Activities are planned in local time; floating time keeps them at the same clock time in any calendar.

data.question: How is money stored?
options: one currency per trip, integer cents
data.answer: one currency per trip, integer cents
data.rationale: Integer cents avoid rounding drift; conversion is out of the first scope.

data.question: Should a completed trip become read-only?
data.rationale: Open: travelers may want to add photos or notes afterwards; the answer does not block the first scope.

data.claim: A trip holds at most 8 travelers and 400 activities.
data.validation_method: A load test with 8 travelers and 400 activities in round 10 keeps every page under 300 ms locally.

data.asset: a family's itinerary behind a share link
data.threat: a guessed, leaked or old token is used
data.impact: a stranger learns where and when a family travels

data.description: 128-bit random tokens, revocation, and one identical not-found answer for unknown and revoked tokens.

data.threat: logs copied to a support channel
data.impact: personal data leaves the family's control

data.description: Logs carry only operational fields; personal fields are removed before writing.
